additional_concerns: All twelve required pairs are retained, including both historical CONTEXT pairs. NOT_APPLICABLE concerns the exact typed question; it neither rejects the supported source claim nor establishes the candidate's overall correctness.

Footnote 3 is present in da12aecad4e68.u30.3569. Its markers attach to the XML and PDF options, not the web form. Both permission claims' missing-footnote statements are stale. The XML statement is supported as a listed-method permission; an alternative reading that treats its extracted conditions as exhaustive sufficient conditions is contradicted by the omitted e-Cert requirement.

The separately provided JFIU XML schema is absent. The circular establishes the obligation to follow it, but not its contents. None of the four opaque dependency IDs identifies that schema, and none has a non-null source_hash; no AVAILABLE assessment or invented dependency mapping is justified.

Both compliance candidates expressly exclude XML-schema conformity from their XML facts. Their TRUE results must remain limited to the selected channel, method and e-Cert control. They do not establish full XML compliance or satisfaction of the separate obligation to liaise with JFIU to arrange a technical test. The source does not expressly make successful completion of that test a precondition to each filing.

Footnote 3 requires a Hongkong Post e-Cert without specifying its operational use. The submission-specific supplied-or-used requirement in node.e527b70be44a95d97a2e5ae5 may implement that requirement, but the packet does not establish the added operational interpretation or establish that possession alone is insufficient. What JFIU instructions define satisfaction of the e-Cert requirement? Those instructions are missing and have no identifiable supplied dependency mapping.

The prescribed PDF form is missing external material needed to assess the completed-prescribed-PDF classifications. Which prescribed form or specification governs the submission, and which dependency ID identifies it? No supplied mapping resolves this.

The date-only trigger in node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 includes the portion of 2 February 2026 before 9:00am. The source separately gives a date-effective channel rule, a 9:00am operational launch and resubmission following implementation. The calendar-date and operational-launch interpretations remain distinct; the date-only predicate cannot distinguish that morning's blackout from the launch.

The timestamp candidates choose an inclusive operational-launch boundary. The packet does not expressly state the governing timezone or definitively resolve how the date-effective provision relates to 'following its implementation' at the exact launch instant. What authoritative clarification resolves these temporal classifications? No supplied dependency ID identifies such clarification.

The blackout provision directs urgent filers to contact JFIU. Contact alone does not establish submission of an STR, but an actual submission resulting from that contact must be assessed on its evidence. Do not generalize post-launch channel exclusivity into the blackout or treat migration as a new original submission.

Non-filing events return FALSE in node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb when its licensed-firm scope holds and facts are nonconflicting, whereas the other event candidates place actual filing in scope and return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Preserve this domain distinction instead of treating the candidates as equivalent.

The history candidate answers whether a qualifying event existed, not whether a duty remains outstanding after later resubmission. Its existential assessment is supplied externally; the formula does not inspect history. FALSE needs enough historical evidence to exclude qualifying events.

The circular promises JFIU resubmission guidance, but that guidance is absent. Which guidance governs performance of the resubmission duty, and which dependency ID identifies it? Its absence does not erase the expressly stated trigger or make unrelated method permissions relevant to that trigger.

Rule-wide conflict blocking can prevent evaluation even when an alternative method would otherwise suffice. This is a declared runtime policy, not an additional substantive restriction established by the circular. Missing classifications, conflicts and unresolved temporal facts must retain their declared non-Boolean outcomes.
